subject: Post-demo: customer-data handling & support access runbook
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Soto <miguel@aurora-pay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: customer-data handling & support access runbook

Hi Miguel — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + proposed runbook items based on the questions from your security and product team: 

Key asks I captured from the call:
- PII classification & per-field handling (what we consider PII vs metadata)
- Per-customer retention controls (ability to set TTLs per account)
- Audit/operational logging retention (who sees what, for how long)
- Support access: RBAC, break-glass, approval workflow and evidence for audits
- Data residency: EU node requirement for some customers

Proposed answers & immediate next steps (high-level):
1) PII and retention: Redwood supports configurable retention windows per-customer. Out of the box we provide 30/90/365 presets, and we can enable a custom TTL tied to the customer ID. We store classification metadata alongside records so that purge jobs target only data marked as PII.

2) Logging: Operational logs (request/response metadata) are retained by default for 180 days in hosted, with options to extend up to 3 years (enterprise plan). Access logs are immutable and tied to request IDs. We can export logs to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Logstash).

3) RBAC & least privilege: Recommended model — 4 roles: Admin (customer-managed), Team Admin, Support (restricted), Auditor (read-only). Support access is time-bound and ticketed; default support sessions require an active ticket and are scoped to the minimum resource set.

4) Break-glass: We propose a break-glass process that requires:
   - a support ticket (JIRA ID)
   - approval from a customer security owner (email + audit trail) or two internal approvers for emergency cases
   - an automatically generated audit bundle (who accessed, what was viewed, duration) exported to the customer's S3 for retention

5) Data residency: We can pin customer workloads to EU-only nodes. For Aurora specifically, we can map your EU tenants to our eu-west endpoints; encryption-at-rest and in-transit meet AES-256/TLS1.3 standards.

Attachments: demo-data-flow.png (high-level flow), support-breakglass-runbook-v1.docx (detailed draft runbook)

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll share the runbook doc (attached) and a short answers doc for your security team by EOD tomorrow.
- Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up next week for a live walkthrough with your security lead? Suggested slots: Wed 5/26 10-11am PT or Thu 5/27 9-11am PT.

If there are any immediate deal-blockers (EU residency SLA, per-field deletion, or an SOC2 AIC requirement), flag and I’ll escalate to our security engineering lead.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Miguel Soto <miguel@aurora-pay.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Pay Security <security@aurora-pay.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: customer-data handling & support access runbook

Priya — appreciate the fast recap. A few clarifying points from our security team: 

- Residency: We need EU-only processing and storage for EU merchant accounts; can you confirm separation of keys and that backups are also EU-only?
- Per-field deletion: We require per-customer per-field deletion calls (can redact PII within a conversation, not just full-record TTL). Is that supported?
- Break-glass notification: We need customers to be notified within 15 minutes of any break-glass event and a signed attestation for emergency accesses.

We attached Aurora's security questionnaire (short list) — if you can return answers to the 8 rows marked "blocker" that would be great. Also timeline: we have a security review window next Wed (6/2) and would need evidence before then to move to procurement.

Thanks —
Miguel Soto
Head of Integrations, Aurora Pay
miguel@aurora-pay.com

--

- aurora-security-reqs.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Soto <miguel@aurora-pay.com>, Aurora Pay Security <security@aurora-pay.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: customer-data handling & support access runbook

Folks — forwarding Miguel's follow-up and Aurora's questionnaire. Below are proposed concrete responses we can send back (drafting here so we keep a single source of truth):

1) EU-only processing & backups:
- We offer tenant pinning to EU physical zones. Keys: we can integrate with your KMS via customer-managed key (bring-your-own-key) so encryption keys never leave the EU. Backups are retained in-region when tenant is pinned.

2) Per-field deletion (granular PII erase):
- Supported. We expose a per-record API that accepts a deletion spec (field-level selectors or regex on field names). Deletions are irreversible and we can provide a signed deletion manifest for audit. Implementation note: per-field deletes run asynchronously; we provide a job id and completion webhook.

3) Break-glass timeline & attestation:
- We can implement the 15-minute notification SLA. Proposed mechanism: when break-glass is invoked, an automated email + webhook is sent to the customer's security contact; we also generate a signed attestation PDF summarizing the access (who, why, duration) and store it in the tenant's evidence folder. For emergencies, we require two internal approvers OR the customer's pre-approved emergency contact.

4) Evidence for 6/2 security review:
- I'll attach an evidence pack: runbook + architecture diagram + redaction API spec + SOC2-ready logging excerpt. If security needs a live walk-through, propose Tue 5/31 9am PT.

5) Operational support controls (practical runbook suggestions):
- Short-lived support tokens (max 8 hours) scoped to specific workspace IDs
- Mandatory ticketing integration (JIRA) — access only when linked to active ticket id
- Automatic audit-bundle generation on any elevated access, stored with checksum and tenant metadata

Proposed immediate action items:
- Aditya: can you confirm license tier that unlocks per-customer retention and KMS BYOK? I need an answer before EOD Friday so we can respond to Aurora's procurement window.
- Marissa: please review the runbook doc and call out any legal/SLA redlines.
- Alex: can you prepare a short evidence bundle (arch diagram + sample audit bundle) for the 6/2 review?

I will draft the responses to the 8 blocker rows and send to Miguel by EOD today once I have the tier confirmation. Miguel — thanks for the timeline; we’ll prioritize.

Best —
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
